name: red
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: dark on the cloth of a person

text: Fairyland and the world of the Otherworld were signed by two colors, red and green. Trooping fairies wore red as a mark of their kind. Solitary fairies kept to green in their own. The red color also held a dark note in folk belief. A dress of red felt like a bad sign for a person, and in the west of Ireland a woman kept away from a red petticoat until recent times. Red hair and a red hide on an animal carried the same bad sign. A spirit cow was said to be white with red-tipped ears. A dog or cat born to that coloring ranked as a creature of the fairy blood. A person with red hair also faced a link to the fairies. To meet a red-haired woman at dawn would darken the day. To pass a man dressed in red as one began a task could spell failure.

okr.objective: Red is one of the two colors that sign the Fairy world.
key_results: Fairyland keeps two colors, red and green.
